ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: From the attached graph, f(t) is nonzero only on two line segments: one segment rises from 0 at t = -T/2 to +1/2 just to the left of t = 0, and the other segment rises from -1/2 just to the right of t = 0 to 0 at t = T/2. The graph is real-valued. The left-side positive segment and the right-side negative segment are negatives of each other under the reflection t -> -t, so f(-t) = -f(t) except possibly at the single point t = 0, which does not affect the Fourier transform. Therefore f(t) is a real odd signal. By the Fourier-transform symmetry property, the Fourier transform of a real odd time-domain function is purely imaginary and odd as a function of ω.

method.method_draft: First describe the graph and note the symmetric support [-T/2,T/2] and odd real waveform. Write F(ω)=∫ f(t)cos(ωt)dt - j∫ f(t)sin(ωt)dt over the support. Since f(t) is odd and cos(ωt) is even, f(t)cos(ωt) is odd, so the real part integral is zero. Since sin(ωt) is odd, f(t)sin(ωt) is even, so the remaining term is purely imaginary. Finally replace ω by -ω: the sine integral changes sign while the cosine part remains zero, so F(-ω)=-F(ω). Therefore F(ω) is imaginary and odd.
